findings.finding: H1 2026 constant-currency growth was about 10.4% (Q1 +8.1% cc on $228.3M; Q2 +12.7% cc on $240.1M, with Europe & International +18% cc on +16.9% volume). The company raised the FY cc guide only to +8-10% (from +3-5%), which implies an H2 slowdown to about +6-9% cc. Q3 2025's comparison base was soft (+3.8% cc, $222.8M), so a second raise or a revenue beat is plausible. The company raised its guide by 5 points on 2026-07-22.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-22 (Q2: revenue $240.1M against a ~$220M consensus, FY revenue guide raised from +3-5% to +8-10% cc): stock +19.1%. 2026-04-29 (Q1, revenue beat, guide reiterated): +3.7%. Q3 2025 (2025-10-29): revenue beat by about $11.8M, reaction not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock is 25% below its 52-week high and fell 7.4% in the five sessions into the print, so it is not trading as if a second raise were expected. The only FY revenue consensus visible ($919.65M) sits below the guided range, which suggests estimates lag the guide. If a raise were priced, the stock would sit nearer the post-Q2 highs.

findings.finding: To reach even the low end of the unchanged FY adjusted-EBITDA guide ($25-35M; management said toward the low end), H2 needs about $20M after H1's $5.4M (Q1 $5.0M, Q2 $0.4M), i.e. roughly $10M a quarter. Q3 2025 was $3.1M. Management also said Middle East fuel, packaging and logistics costs will run in Q3 and Q4 'broadly in line with' Q2, and that growth reinvestment continues at only a 'slightly lower' level. That makes a Q3 EBITDA shortfall or an EBITDA guide cut the main downside line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITDA guide was held at the low end on 2026-07-22 and the stock still rose 19.1% on revenue. No case was found of an EBITDA guide cut in 2026. In 2025 the Q3 EPS miss (-$2.00 vs est.) was driven by convertible-note fair-value losses; the reaction is not sourced.
findings.why_not_priced: The low-end steer is public, so part of this is priced. The H1-to-H2 arithmetic ($5.4M to about $20M, against a $3.1M Q3 last year) is not laid out in any wire copy found. If it were priced, the put/call ratio and the 5-day slide would be larger. The 5-day -7.4% may be partial pricing.
findings.independence: The guide and the H1 EBITDA come from the company's own Q1 and Q2 releases (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843586/000184358626000015/otly-ex99_1.htm). The Q3 2025 base of $3.1M comes from https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/10/29/3176290/0/en/Oatly-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results.html. All of these are company documents, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: Balance sheet at 2026-06-30: cash $44.6M (from $64.3M at YE2025), current interest-bearing borrowings $344.4M (vs $340.3M at YE, so the current classification is structural and not new), total equity -$23.5M (negative, from +$19.7M). Management guides no positive FCF for 2026 because of an H2 inventory build and capex, and says the plan is 'fully funded'. The Q3 cash print will show how far cash runs down. Asked what the money buys: inventory for a volume ramp (E&I volume +16.9%), so this is a near-zero negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Nordic bond listing prospectus on 2026-09-24 coincided with a -2.4% move, but that was not an earnings event.
findings.why_not_priced: The negative equity and the current-debt line sit in the 6-K balance sheet, not the press release, so they are little read. But the balance was already similar at YE2025, so this is mostly known; the size is small for that reason.
findings.independence: The Q1 6-K showed the same structure ($337.4M current borrowings, $49.4M cash): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843586/000184358626000015/otly-ex99_1.htm. Same issuer's filings, not independent.

findings.finding: The Greater China strategic review (possible carve-out) is ongoing, with completion 'intended before year-end 2026' per the Q2 call. The company will not update unless the Board approves a course of action, so the Q3 release or call is a natural place for an outcome. The GC segment runs at negative adjusted EBITDA (Q1 -$0.8M, Q2 -$1.5M) on about 13% of revenue, so a carve-out or sale would lift group margins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: the review has been open since July 2025 with no outcome announced.
findings.why_not_priced: The timing is a year-end-2026 target, so the probability that an outcome lands at this print is uncertain and the market is likely to assign it little weight. If an announcement were expected, the options would trade a wider event premium; they are already wide, but on a thin, 50%-spread chain.
findings.independence: Q2 call (2026-07-22) confirms completion intended before YE2026: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/22/oatly-otly-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/

findings.finding: North America: management said on 2026-07-22 that the lost-foodservice-customer headwind has 'substantially ended', TDPs rose from 17% to 22%, and ACV from about 32% toward about 50%, with retailers adding new products outside the normal reset window from late Q3 2026. Q2 NA revenue was $66.9M, +5.9% cc. NA is about 28% of revenue; Europe & International (about 60%) has to keep growing double digits for the total to clear the guide, and Q2 shows it did.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NA returned to growth in Q2 (+5.9% cc) in the quarter the stock rose 19.1%. Q1 NA was +3.7% cc (stock +3.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: The distribution gains are stated on the call and are not in the headline numbers, and the 'retail category growth remains soft' caveat keeps expectations low. If they were priced, the stock would not have given back about 7% over the last week.
findings.independence: Q2 segment table: https://quartr.com/events/oatly-group-ab-otly-q2-2026_3sKY5lZw. It is the same company disclosure, so not fully independent.

findings.finding: Input-cost proxy: the EU composite feed-oat price was about EUR 166.84/t in October 2026, roughly 17% below a year earlier, and the 2026 German harvest was near the multi-year average. Oats are a modest share of Oatly's COGS, which is dominated by packaging, logistics and energy, and purchases are contracted ahead, so the transmission to Q3 is small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Gross margin rose 140bp in Q2 (33.9%) and 190bp in Q1.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar unsourced): no Q3 consensus, so the guidance-raise finding was capped from +2.5 to +2.0 and NA from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 6 (inside what was guided): the EBITDA low-end steer is already public, so the EBITDA finding went from -2.0 to -1.5.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the cash burn funds an H2 inventory build for a volume ramp, so the balance-sheet finding went from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth about 0): the positioning finding went from +0.5 to +0.2.
Greater China timing uncertain (target is YE2026, not necessarily this print): +1.0 to +0.8.
